explanation: `items[len(items)]` indexes one position past the last valid index — for a list of length n, valid indices run from 0 to n-1, so `len(items)` is out of range and raises an IndexError. It should be `items[len(items) - 1]` (or simply `items[-1]`).
prompt: This function is supposed to return the last element of a list. What's actually wrong with it?
choices: `len(items)` is one past the last valid index, so this raises an IndexError instead of returning the last element
The function forgot to import the `len` builtin before using it
Lists in Python only support 0-based indexing for slices, not for direct element access, so this always fails
The parameter name `items` shadows a Python builtin and causes a runtime error
